                - heading [level=3] [ref=f3e147]:

                  - text: ", an AI voice agent built for the mortgage industry. It offers instant lead engagement and warm transfers to live agents. Vox increases lead conversion, streamlines pre-qualification, and integrates with your CRM while meeting regulatory standards."
                - heading [level=3] [ref=f3e144]:
                  - strong [ref=f3e145]: The Problem
                - paragraph [ref=f3e146]: As interest rates change, demand for mortgages fluctuates dramatically. Mortgage lenders need to have a crystal ball to predict the exact timing of these moves and hire well ahead of a spike in demand. If that spike doesn’t come, money is wasted hiring and training unneeded staff. If hiring is not done early enough, then revenue is left on the table when the mortgage lender cannot service the demand.
                - heading [level=3] [ref=f3e147]:
                  - strong [ref=f3e148]: The Solution
                - paragraph [ref=f3e149]: At Marr Labs we just announced the launch of Vox Mortgage, an AI voice agent designed specifically for the mortgage industry. Vox enables mortgage lenders to contact borrowers in milliseconds, offering human-like interactions and rapid lead engagement.               - paragraph [ref=f6e161]: Before we joined YC, we worked at a supply chain unicorn startup called Stord where our jobs involved making their warehouse shipping facility run efficiently. While we were there, we realized that operations still largely relied on paper to pack an order correctly. Let me explain what actually happens in the warehouse when you order something from Walmart…
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e162]:
                - strong [ref=f6e163]: 🎯 TL;DR
              - paragraph [ref=f6e164]: Every time workers in a warehouse box an order, they are supposed to reference 100+ page manuals that include precise packing instructions like where to put the shipping label. It’s not practical for warehouse workers to check the manuals on every order, and thus mistakes happen. These mistakes result in hefty fines, amounting to $40B annually! RetailReady’s mobile application replaces the paper manuals, making it easy to stay compliant and mitigate these fines, without any training time or integrations required.
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e165]:
                - text: 🔍
                - strong [ref=f6e166]: Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f6e167]: Retailers (e.g. Walmart, Amazon, Target) outline unique shipping requirements for brands (think Dove, Hanes, Stanley) through 100+ page manuals called routing guides. If retailers receive a non-compliant shipment such as incorrect label placement, they issue brands a compliance violation fee, called chargebacks.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e168]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e169]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e170]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e171]: An example from page 227/399 of Walmart’s guidelines…
              - paragraph [ref=f6e172]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e173]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e174]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e175]: …And how these shipping guidelines manifest on the warehouse floor today
              - paragraph [ref=f6e176]:
                - text: On average, 3% of a brand’s gross invoice amount is deducted due to chargebacks, resulting in an estimated
                - strong [ref=f6e177]: $40B worth of retailer chargebacks per year.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e178]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e179]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e180]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e181]: A subsection of violation fees outlined in a retailer routing guide
              - paragraph [ref=f6e182]:
                - text: On the flip side, when retailers receive these orders from brands, their warehouse team also uses their own printed routing guides to determine whether or not a shipment is compliant, and then manually enter associated fines into a spreadsheet. 10-12% of all orders retailers receive are deemed non-compliant and
                - strong [ref=f6e183]: require 2X the labor time
                - text: .

                - strong [ref=f6e185]: 🦾 Solution
              - paragraph [ref=f6e186]: RetailReady is the ultimate retail compliance solution for all stakeholders, requiring no training time or integrations.

                - strong [ref=f6e188]: "Third-Party Logistics (3PLs):"

              - paragraph [ref=f6e191]:
                - strong [ref=f6e192]: "Brands:"

                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e194]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e195]:
                - strong [ref=f6e196]: "Retailers:"
                - text: Our retailer mobile app automatically detects and records shipping compliance errors from vendors, speeding up revenue generation and increasing labor efficiency.

              - paragraph [ref=f6e161]: Before we joined YC, we worked at a supply chain unicorn startup called Stord where our jobs involved making their warehouse shipping facility run efficiently. While we were there, we realized that operations still largely relied on paper to pack an order correctly. Let me explain what actually happens in the warehouse when you order something from Walmart…
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e162]:
                - strong [ref=f6e163]: 🎯 TL;DR
              - paragraph [ref=f6e164]: Every time workers in a warehouse box an order, they are supposed to reference 100+ page manuals that include precise packing instructions like where to put the shipping label. It’s not practical for warehouse workers to check the manuals on every order, and thus mistakes happen. These mistakes result in hefty fines, amounting to $40B annually! RetailReady’s mobile application replaces the paper manuals, making it easy to stay compliant and mitigate these fines, without any training time or integrations required.
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e165]:
                - text: 🔍
                - strong [ref=f6e166]: Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f6e167]: Retailers (e.g. Walmart, Amazon, Target) outline unique shipping requirements for brands (think Dove, Hanes, Stanley) through 100+ page manuals called routing guides. If retailers receive a non-compliant shipment such as incorrect label placement, they issue brands a compliance violation fee, called chargebacks.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e168]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e169]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e170]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e171]: An example from page 227/399 of Walmart’s guidelines…
              - paragraph [ref=f6e172]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e173]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e174]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e175]: …And how these shipping guidelines manifest on the warehouse floor today
              - paragraph [ref=f6e176]:
                - text: On average, 3% of a brand’s gross invoice amount is deducted due to chargebacks, resulting in an estimated
                - strong [ref=f6e177]: $40B worth of retailer chargebacks per year.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e178]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e179]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e180]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e181]: A subsection of violation fees outlined in a retailer routing guide
              - paragraph [ref=f6e182]:
                - text: On the flip side, when retailers receive these orders from brands, their warehouse team also uses their own printed routing guides to determine whether or not a shipment is compliant, and then manually enter associated fines into a spreadsheet. 10-12% of all orders retailers receive are deemed non-compliant and
                - strong [ref=f6e183]: require 2X the labor time

                - strong [ref=f6e185]: 🦾 Solution
              - paragraph [ref=f6e186]: RetailReady is the ultimate retail compliance solution for all stakeholders, requiring no training time or integrations.

                - strong [ref=f6e188]: "Third-Party Logistics (3PLs):"
                - text: Our user-friendly mobile application ensures operational shipping compliance to retailers. Our software ingests retailer routing guides and translates them into step-by-step workflow tasks while providing a visual repository of every order for dispute resolution.

              - paragraph [ref=f6e191]:
                - strong [ref=f6e192]: "Brands:"

              - paragraph [ref=f6e195]:
                - strong [ref=f6e196]: "Retailers:"
                - text: Our retailer mobile app automatically detects and records shipping compliance errors from vendors, speeding up revenue generation and increasing labor efficiency.

              - paragraph [ref=f6e161]: Before we joined YC, we worked at a supply chain unicorn startup called Stord where our jobs involved making their warehouse shipping facility run efficiently. While we were there, we realized that operations still largely relied on paper to pack an order correctly. Let me explain what actually happens in the warehouse when you order something from Walmart…
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e162]:
                - strong [ref=f6e163]: 🎯 TL;DR
              - paragraph [ref=f6e164]: Every time workers in a warehouse box an order, they are supposed to reference 100+ page manuals that include precise packing instructions like where to put the shipping label. It’s not practical for warehouse workers to check the manuals on every order, and thus mistakes happen. These mistakes result in hefty fines, amounting to $40B annually! RetailReady’s mobile application replaces the paper manuals, making it easy to stay compliant and mitigate these fines, without any training time or integrations required.
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e165]:
                - text: 🔍
                - strong [ref=f6e166]: Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f6e167]: Retailers (e.g. Walmart, Amazon, Target) outline unique shipping requirements for brands (think Dove, Hanes, Stanley) through 100+ page manuals called routing guides. If retailers receive a non-compliant shipment such as incorrect label placement, they issue brands a compliance violation fee, called chargebacks.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e168]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e169]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e170]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e171]: An example from page 227/399 of Walmart’s guidelines…
              - paragraph [ref=f6e172]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e173]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e174]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e175]: …And how these shipping guidelines manifest on the warehouse floor today
              - paragraph [ref=f6e176]:
                - text: On average, 3% of a brand’s gross invoice amount is deducted due to chargebacks, resulting in an estimated
                - strong [ref=f6e177]: $40B worth of retailer chargebacks per year.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e178]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e179]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e180]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e181]: A subsection of violation fees outlined in a retailer routing guide
              - paragraph [ref=f6e182]:
                - text: On the flip side, when retailers receive these orders from brands, their warehouse team also uses their own printed routing guides to determine whether or not a shipment is compliant, and then manually enter associated fines into a spreadsheet. 10-12% of all orders retailers receive are deemed non-compliant and
                - strong [ref=f6e183]: require 2X the labor time
                - text: .
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e184]:
                - strong [ref=f6e185]: 🦾 Solution
              - paragraph [ref=f6e186]: RetailReady is the ultimate retail compliance solution for all stakeholders, requiring no training time or integrations.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e187]:
                - strong [ref=f6e188]: "Third-Party Logistics (3PLs):"
                - text: Our user-friendly mobile application ensures operational shipping compliance to retailers. Our software ingests retailer routing guides and translates them into step-by-step workflow tasks while providing a visual repository of every order for dispute resolution.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e189]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e190]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e191]:
                - strong [ref=f6e192]: "Brands:"
                - text: Our dashboard offers insights into your or your 3PL's operations, allowing you to upload chargebacks. This data enhances our model, tailoring your packing process with extra validation checks.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e193]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e194]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e195]:
                - strong [ref=f6e196]: "Retailers:"
                - text: Our retailer mobile app automatically detects and records shipping compliance errors from vendors, speeding up revenue generation and increasing labor efficiency.

              - heading [level=1]
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e159]:
                - strong [ref=f6e160]: ⏪ Backstory
              - paragraph [ref=f6e161]: Before we joined YC, we worked at a supply chain unicorn startup called Stord where our jobs involved making their warehouse shipping facility run efficiently. While we were there, we realized that operations still largely relied on paper to pack an order correctly. Let me explain what actually happens in the warehouse when you order something from Walmart…
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e162]:
                - strong [ref=f6e163]: 🎯 TL;DR
              - paragraph [ref=f6e164]: Every time workers in a warehouse box an order, they are supposed to reference 100+ page manuals that include precise packing instructions like where to put the shipping label. It’s not practical for warehouse workers to check the manuals on every order, and thus mistakes happen. These mistakes result in hefty fines, amounting to $40B annually! RetailReady’s mobile application replaces the paper manuals, making it easy to stay compliant and mitigate these fines, without any training time or integrations required.
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e165]:
                - text: 🔍
                - strong [ref=f6e166]: Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f6e167]: Retailers (e.g. Walmart, Amazon, Target) outline unique shipping requirements for brands (think Dove, Hanes, Stanley) through 100+ page manuals called routing guides. If retailers receive a non-compliant shipment such as incorrect label placement, they issue brands a compliance violation fee, called chargebacks.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e168]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e169]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e170]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e171]: An example from page 227/399 of Walmart’s guidelines…
              - paragraph [ref=f6e172]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e173]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e174]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e175]: …And how these shipping guidelines manifest on the warehouse floor today
              - paragraph [ref=f6e176]:
                - text: On average, 3% of a brand’s gross invoice amount is deducted due to chargebacks, resulting in an estimated
                - strong [ref=f6e177]: $40B worth of retailer chargebacks per year.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e178]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e179]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e180]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e181]: A subsection of violation fees outlined in a retailer routing guide
              - paragraph [ref=f6e182]:
                - text: On the flip side, when retailers receive these orders from brands, their warehouse team also uses their own printed routing guides to determine whether or not a shipment is compliant, and then manually enter associated fines into a spreadsheet. 10-12% of all orders retailers receive are deemed non-compliant and
                - strong [ref=f6e183]: require 2X the labor time
                - text: .
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e184]:
                - strong [ref=f6e185]: 🦾 Solution
              - paragraph [ref=f6e186]: RetailReady is the ultimate retail compliance solution for all stakeholders, requiring no training time or integrations.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e187]:
                - strong [ref=f6e188]: "Third-Party Logistics (3PLs):"
                - text: Our user-friendly mobile application ensures operational shipping compliance to retailers. Our software ingests retailer routing guides and translates them into step-by-step workflow tasks while providing a visual repository of every order for dispute resolution.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e189]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e190]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e191]:
                - strong [ref=f6e192]: "Brands:"
                - text: Our dashboard offers insights into your or your 3PL's operations, allowing you to upload chargebacks. This data enhances our model, tailoring your packing process with extra validation checks.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e193]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e194]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e195]:
                - strong [ref=f6e196]: "Retailers:"
                - text: Our retailer mobile app automatically detects and records shipping compliance errors from vendors, speeding up revenue generation and increasing labor efficiency.
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e197]:
                - strong [ref=f6e198]: 👋Our Ask
              - list [ref=f6e199]:
                - listitem [ref=f6e200]:
                  - text: If you know any brands / 3PLs that are struggling with retailer compliance or retailers that are struggling with vendor compliance, we’d love warm intros! Email us at
                  - link "founders@retailreadyai.com" [ref=f6e201]:

                - listitem [ref=f6e202]:
                  - text: If you are a brand / 3PL / retailer that is interested in our solution,

                  - text: a demo with us!

                  - listitem [ref=f7e142]: Iterate on your categories till you’re set.

              - paragraph [ref=f10e138]:
                - strong [ref=f10e139]: TL;DR
                - text: ": SiLogy is building a platform for chip developers to run tests, track test statistics, and collaborate on debugging."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e140]: —
              - paragraph [ref=f10e141]:
                - text: Hey, we’re
                - link "Paul" [ref=f10e142]:
                  - /url: https://linkedin.com/in/paul-kim-7b766262
                - text: and
                - link "Kay" [ref=f10e143]:

                - link "SiLogy" [ref=f10e144]:
                  - /url: https://silogy.io
                - text: . We’re building chip design and verification tools to speed up the semiconductor development cycle.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e145]:
                - strong [ref=f10e146]: The Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f10e147]:
                - text: Interest in designing new chips is growing, thanks to demand from AI and the predicted decline of Moore’s Law. Since the number of possible states grows exponentially with chip complexity, the need for testing in simulation is exploding, with chip developers already spending 70% of their time on testing. (See this video on the
                - link "verification gap" [ref=f10e148]:
                  - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rtaaOdGuMCc
                - text: ).

                                - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rtaaOdGuMCc
                              - link "Asianometry" [ref=f11e22] [cursor=pointer]:

                              - generic [ref=f11e43]: Watch on
              - paragraph [ref=f10e151]: Tooling hasn’t kept up. The state-of-the-art in collaborative debugging is to walk to a coworker’s desk and point to an error in a log file or waveform file. Each chip company rolls out its own tooling and infra to deal with this—this was Kay’s entire job at his last gig. But they want to work on chips, not devtools! The solutions they come up with are often inadequate and frustrating. That’s why we started SiLogy.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e152]:
                - strong [ref=f10e153]: The solution
              - paragraph [ref=f10e154]: SiLogy is a web app to manage the entire digital verification workflow. (“Digital verification” means testing the logic of the design and includes everything before the physical design of the chip. It’s the most time-consuming stage in verification.)
              - paragraph [ref=f10e155]: "We combine three capabilities:"
              - paragraph [ref=f10e156]:
                - strong [ref=f10e157]: Test running, results, and statistics
                - text: ": Our CI tool runs tests in the cloud, allowing engineering teams unlimited flexibility in scaling their test volume. We also track each project’s progress in test coverage and test pass rate."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e158]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e159]
              - paragraph [ref=f10e160]:
                - strong [ref=f10e161]: Killer application-specific features
                - text: ": We’re building features tailored for verification use cases. We incorporate a test orchestration framework, waveform viewer, coverage report, and other features specifically for verification teams, providing customers an advantage over competitors using a generic CI solution such as Jenkins."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e162]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e163]
              - paragraph [ref=f10e164]:
                - strong [ref=f10e165]: Collaboration
                - text: ": soon you’ll be able to send a link to and leave a comment on a specific location within a log or waveform file, just like in Google Docs."

                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e167]
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e168]:
                - strong [ref=f10e169]: Asks

If that spike doesn’t come, money is wasted hiring and training unneeded staff. If hiring is not done early enough, then revenue is left on the table when the mortgage lender cannot service the demand.
                - heading [level=3] [ref=f3e147]:
                  - strong [ref=f3e148]: The Solution
                - paragraph [ref=f3e149]: At Marr Labs we just announced the launch of Vox Mortgage, an AI voice agent designed specifically for the mortgage industry. Vox enables mortgage lenders to contact borrowers in milliseconds, offering human-like interactions and rapid lead engagement. The AI voice agent’s standout feature is its warm transfer capability, ensuring a smooth handoff from AI to live agents, increasing conversion rates and minimizing call abandonment.
                - paragraph [ref=f3e150]: "Vox Mortgage was created to address two crucial challenges in the mortgage industry: speed and seamless customer experience. Not only does Vox engage leads within milliseconds, but our warm transfer technology ensures a smooth transition to live agents, enhancing the borrower’s experience and boosting conversion rates."
                - paragraph [ref=f3e151]: Best of all, Vox Mortgage has unlimited scalability, allowing mortgage lenders to easily scale to make or receive as many calls a day as needed–all with no fixed costs.

              - paragraph [ref=f6e161]: Before we joined YC, we worked at a supply chain unicorn startup called Stord where our jobs involved making their warehouse shipping facility run efficiently. While we were there, we realized that operations still largely relied on paper to pack an order correctly. Let me explain what actually happens in the warehouse when you order something from Walmart…
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e162]:
                - strong [ref=f6e163]: 🎯 TL;DR
              - paragraph [ref=f6e164]: Every time workers in a warehouse box an order, they are supposed to reference 100+ page manuals that include precise packing instructions like where to put the shipping label. It’s not practical for warehouse workers to check the manuals on every order, and thus mistakes happen. These mistakes result in hefty fines, amounting to $40B annually! RetailReady’s mobile application replaces the paper manuals, making it easy to stay compliant and mitigate these fines, without any training time or integrations required.
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e165]:
                - text: 🔍
                - strong [ref=f6e166]: Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f6e167]: Retailers (e.g. Walmart, Amazon, Target) outline unique shipping requirements for brands (think Dove, Hanes, Stanley) through 100+ page manuals called routing guides. If retailers receive a non-compliant shipment such as incorrect label placement, they issue brands a compliance violation fee, called chargebacks.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e168]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e169]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e170]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e171]: An example from page 227/399 of Walmart’s guidelines…
              - paragraph [ref=f6e172]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e173]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e174]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e175]: …And how these shipping guidelines manifest on the warehouse floor today
              - paragraph [ref=f6e176]:
                - text: On average, 3% of a brand’s gross invoice amount is deducted due to chargebacks, resulting in an estimated
                - strong [ref=f6e177]: $40B worth of retailer chargebacks per year.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e178]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e179]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e180]:
                - emphasis [ref=f6e181]: A subsection of violation fees outlined in a retailer routing guide
              - paragraph [ref=f6e182]:
                - text: On the flip side, when retailers receive these orders from brands, their warehouse team also uses their own printed routing guides to determine whether or not a shipment is compliant, and then manually enter associated fines into a spreadsheet. 10-12% of all orders retailers receive are deemed non-compliant and
                - strong [ref=f6e183]: require 2X the labor time
                - text: .
              - heading [level=1] [ref=f6e184]:
                - strong [ref=f6e185]: 🦾 Solution
              - paragraph [ref=f6e186]: RetailReady is the ultimate retail compliance solution for all stakeholders, requiring no training time or integrations.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e187]:
                - strong [ref=f6e188]: "Third-Party Logistics (3PLs):"
                - text: Our user-friendly mobile application ensures operational shipping compliance to retailers. Our software ingests retailer routing guides and translates them into step-by-step workflow tasks while providing a visual repository of every order for dispute resolution.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e189]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e190]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e191]:
                - strong [ref=f6e192]: "Brands:"
                - text: Our dashboard offers insights into your or your 3PL's operations, allowing you to upload chargebacks. This data enhances our model, tailoring your packing process with extra validation checks.
              - paragraph [ref=f6e193]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f6e194]
              - paragraph [ref=f6e195]:
                - strong [ref=f6e196]: "Retailers:"
                - text: Our retailer mobile app automatically detects and records shipping compliance errors from vendors, speeding up revenue generation and increasing labor efficiency.

            - generic [ref=f13e140]:

            - generic [ref=f13e146]:
              - heading [level=3] [ref=f13e147]:
                - strong [ref=f13e148]: What is a brain foundation model?
              - paragraph [ref=f13e149]: We are building a foundation model, from the ground up, trained on a massive and diverse corpus of brainwave data i.e. Electroencephalography (EEG). In other words, similar to how Large Language Models (LLM) are trained on human language ie. text, our model is trained on brain language ie. brainwaves.
              - paragraph [ref=f13e150]:
                - text: Our foundation model will be able to understand and detect the many facets of brain activity, from disease to wellbeing. Crucially,
                - strong [ref=f13e151]: similar to how ChatGPT can be fine-tuned to become a lawyer or a python developer, our brain foundation model will easily be fine-tuned to become a neurologist co-pilot or a biomarker discovery assistant.
                - text: And, this is only our first milestone - more on this below.
              - paragraph [ref=f13e152]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f13e153]
              - heading [level=3] [ref=f13e154]:
                - strong [ref=f13e155]: The opportunity
              - paragraph [ref=f13e156]: "Our brain foundation model will address a variety of use cases with minimal training, such as:"
              - list [ref=f13e157]:
                - listitem [ref=f13e158]:
                  - strong [ref=f13e159]: Diagnosis
                  - text: of a vast majority of neurological conditions.
                - listitem [ref=f13e160]:
                  - text: Drug and
                  - strong [ref=f13e161]: biomarker discovery
                  - text: in clinical trials.
                - listitem [ref=f13e162]:
                  - strong [ref=f13e163]: Remote monitoring
                  - text: of brainwave abnormalities, e.g., treatment response to drugs or sleep irregularities.
                - listitem [ref=f13e164]:
                  - text: Real-time tracking of brain health, such as cognition or head injuries, measured through
                  - strong [ref=f13e165]: helmets in sports and military
                  - text: .
                - listitem [ref=f13e166]:
                  - text: Empowering devices such as
                  - strong [ref=f13e167]: Apple Vision Pro and Meta Quest
                  - text: to translate brain signals into everyday actions.
              - heading [level=3] [ref=f13e168]:
                - strong [ref=f13e169]: Why are we starting with neurological conditions?
              - paragraph [ref=f13e170]: "During his PhD at London's St Thomas' EEG department, Dimitris discovered a key insight: EEG is a crucial test for neurological disorders, but its manual review process is both slow and error-prone. Specifically:"
              - list [ref=f13e171]:
                - listitem [ref=f13e172]:
                  - strong [ref=f13e173]: Neurologists manually inspect the EEG
                  - text: brainwaves to identify abnormal patterns. This can lead to a 30% margin of error and crucially misdiagnoses.
                - listitem [ref=f13e174]:
                  - text: There is a
                  - strong [ref=f13e175]: substantial rise of EEG data
                  - text: being collected, due to the deployment of remote EEG devices. Despite these remote devices continuously recording patients at home, there is no way to review this enormous and continuous stream of incoming data.
                - listitem [ref=f13e176]:
                  - text: Conversely to the upward EEG data trend,
                  - strong [ref=f13e177]: there is an extreme shortage of neurologists
                  - text: leading to wait times lasting several months.

              - paragraph [ref=f6e164]: Every time workers in a warehouse box an order, they are supposed to reference 100+ page manuals that include precise packing instructions like where to put the shipping label.               - paragraph [ref=f10e138]:
                - strong [ref=f10e139]: TL;DR
                - text: ": SiLogy is building a platform for chip developers to run tests, track test statistics, and collaborate on debugging."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e140]: —
              - paragraph [ref=f10e141]:
                - text: Hey, we’re
                - link "Paul" [ref=f10e142]:
                  - /url: https://linkedin.com/in/paul-kim-7b766262
                - text: and
                - link "Kay" [ref=f10e143]:
                  - /url: https://linkedin.com/in/kay-li-84924128b
                - text: ", the cofounders of"
                - link "SiLogy" [ref=f10e144]:
                  - /url: https://silogy.io
                - text: . We’re building chip design and verification tools to speed up the semiconductor development cycle.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e145]:
                - strong [ref=f10e146]: The Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f10e147]:
                - text: Interest in designing new chips is growing, thanks to demand from AI and the predicted decline of Moore’s Law. Since the number of possible states grows exponentially with chip complexity, the need for testing in simulation is exploding, with chip developers already spending 70% of their time on testing. (See this video on the
                - link "verification gap" [ref=f10e148]:
                  - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rtaaOdGuMCc
                - text: ).

                                - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rtaaOdGuMCc
                              - link "Asianometry" [ref=f11e22] [cursor=pointer]:

                              - generic [ref=f11e43]: Watch on
              - paragraph [ref=f10e151]: Tooling hasn’t kept up. The state-of-the-art in collaborative debugging is to walk to a coworker’s desk and point to an error in a log file or waveform file. Each chip company rolls out its own tooling and infra to deal with this—this was Kay’s entire job at his last gig. But they want to work on chips, not devtools! The solutions they come up with are often inadequate and frustrating. That’s why we started SiLogy.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e152]:
                - strong [ref=f10e153]: The solution
              - paragraph [ref=f10e154]: SiLogy is a web app to manage the entire digital verification workflow. (“Digital verification” means testing the logic of the design and includes everything before the physical design of the chip. It’s the most time-consuming stage in verification.)
              - paragraph [ref=f10e155]: "We combine three capabilities:"
              - paragraph [ref=f10e156]:
                - strong [ref=f10e157]: Test running, results, and statistics
                - text: ": Our CI tool runs tests in the cloud, allowing engineering teams unlimited flexibility in scaling their test volume. We also track each project’s progress in test coverage and test pass rate."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e158]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e159]
              - paragraph [ref=f10e160]:
                - strong [ref=f10e161]: Killer application-specific features
                - text: ": We’re building features tailored for verification use cases. We incorporate a test orchestration framework, waveform viewer, coverage report, and other features specifically for verification teams, providing customers an advantage over competitors using a generic CI solution such as Jenkins."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e162]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e163]
              - paragraph [ref=f10e164]:
                - strong [ref=f10e165]: Collaboration
                - text: ": soon you’ll be able to send a link to and leave a comment on a specific location within a log or waveform file, just like in Google Docs."

                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e167]
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e168]:
                - strong [ref=f10e169]: Asks
              - paragraph [ref=f10e170]:
                - text: If you have experience with Verilog, even just from college, give our product a try at

                - text: . Tell your loved ones who work on chip or FPGA design and verification to give us a try as well.

Could we grab 15 minutes on a call in the next week or two? I'd love to hear about the technical roadmap and share a bit about what we're building that could be relevant to your team.

Best,

I'd love to hear more about how brands and 3PLs are responding since your TechCrunch feature.

Would you have 15 minutes for a quick call in the coming weeks? I'd appreciate learning more about your rollout and sharing how we might support RetailReady's growth.

Best,

Best,

Best,

Your path from high-frequency trading into chip verification tooling is a fascinating angle on the problem Silogy is solving. With chip developers spending up to 70% of their time on testing, the cloud-based CI and collaboration tools you're building at Silogy seem incredibly timely given the AI-driven surge in chip design.

Would you have 15 minutes for a call in the next week or two? I'd love to hear how adoption is going with verification teams and share a bit about what we're working on.

Best,
[Your Name]"

I'd love to hear more about how engineering teams are using the platform day to day.

Could we set up a brief 15-minute call in the next couple of weeks? I'd appreciate the chance to learn more and share how we might be able to help Silogy grow.

Best,

Dimitris Fotis Sakellariou,https://linkedin.com/in/sacellarius,"Subject: Piramidal's foundation model for EEG

Your background running EEG research for over a decade combined with deep learning experience at IQVIA makes Piramidal's foundation-model approach to brainwave data especially compelling. The idea of a 'neurologist co-pilot' for epilepsy diagnosis addressing the 30% margin of error in manual EEG review is a huge opportunity.

Would you be open to a 15-minute call in the next week or two? I'd love to learn more about your model's progress and share how we might be able to support Piramidal.

Do you have 15 minutes for a quick call in the coming weeks? I'd enjoy learning more about where Piramidal is headed and sharing how we might be able to help.

                - strong [ref=f10e139]: TL;DR
                - text: ": SiLogy is building a platform for chip developers to run tests, track test statistics, and collaborate on debugging."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e140]: —
              - paragraph [ref=f10e141]:
                - text: Hey, we’re
                - link "Paul" [ref=f10e142]:
                  - /url: https://linkedin.com/in/paul-kim-7b766262
                - text: and
                - link "Kay" [ref=f10e143]:

                - link "SiLogy" [ref=f10e144]:
                  - /url: https://silogy.io
                - text: . We’re building chip design and verification tools to speed up the semiconductor development cycle.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e145]:
                - strong [ref=f10e146]: The Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f10e147]:
                - text: Interest in designing new chips is growing, thanks to demand from AI and the predicted decline of Moore’s Law. Since the number of possible states grows exponentially with chip complexity, the need for testing in simulation is exploding, with chip developers already spending 70% of their time on testing. (See this video on the
                - link "verification gap" [ref=f10e148]:
                  - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rtaaOdGuMCc
                - text: ).

              - paragraph [ref=f10e151]: Tooling hasn’t kept up. The state-of-the-art in collaborative debugging is to walk to a coworker’s desk and point to an error in a log file or waveform file. Each chip company rolls out its own tooling and infra to deal with this—this was Kay’s entire job at his last gig. But they want to work on chips, not devtools! The solutions they come up with are often inadequate and frustrating. That’s why we started SiLogy.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e152]:
                - strong [ref=f10e153]: The solution
              - paragraph [ref=f10e154]: SiLogy is a web app to manage the entire digital verification workflow. (“Digital verification” means testing the logic of the design and includes everything before the physical design of the chip. It’s the most time-consuming stage in verification.)
              - paragraph [ref=f10e155]: "We combine three capabilities:"
              - paragraph [ref=f10e156]:
                - strong [ref=f10e157]: Test running, results, and statistics
                - text: ": Our CI tool runs tests in the cloud, allowing engineering teams unlimited flexibility in scaling their test volume. We also track each project’s progress in test coverage and test pass rate."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e158]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e159]
              - paragraph [ref=f10e160]:
                - strong [ref=f10e161]: Killer application-specific features
                - text: ": We’re building features tailored for verification use cases. We incorporate a test orchestration framework, waveform viewer, coverage report, and other features specifically for verification teams, providing customers an advantage over competitors using a generic CI solution such as Jenkins."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e162]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e163]
              - paragraph [ref=f10e164]:
                - strong [ref=f10e165]: Collaboration
                - text: ": soon you’ll be able to send a link to and leave a comment on a specific location within a log or waveform file, just like in Google Docs."

                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e167]
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e168]:
                - strong [ref=f10e169]: Asks
              - paragraph [ref=f10e170]:
                - text: If you have experience with Verilog, even just from college, give our product a try at

                - text: . Tell your loved ones who work on chip or FPGA design and verification to give us a try as well.

              - paragraph [ref=f10e138]:
                - strong [ref=f10e139]: TL;DR
                - text: ": SiLogy is building a platform for chip developers to run tests, track test statistics, and collaborate on debugging."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e140]: —
              - paragraph [ref=f10e141]:
                - text: Hey, we’re
                - link "Paul" [ref=f10e142]:
                  - /url: https://linkedin.com/in/paul-kim-7b766262
                - text: and
                - link "Kay" [ref=f10e143]:
                  - /url: https://linkedin.com/in/kay-li-84924128b
                - text: ", the cofounders of"
                - link "SiLogy" [ref=f10e144]:
                  - /url: https://silogy.io
                - text: . We’re building chip design and verification tools to speed up the semiconductor development cycle.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e145]:
                - strong [ref=f10e146]: The Problem
              - paragraph [ref=f10e147]:
                - text: Interest in designing new chips is growing, thanks to demand from AI and the predicted decline of Moore’s Law. Since the number of possible states grows exponentially with chip complexity, the need for testing in simulation is exploding, with chip developers already spending 70% of their time on testing. (See this video on the
                - link "verification gap" [ref=f10e148]:
                  - /url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rtaaOdGuMCc
                - text: ).

                              - generic [ref=f11e43]: Watch on
              - paragraph [ref=f10e151]: Tooling hasn’t kept up. The state-of-the-art in collaborative debugging is to walk to a coworker’s desk and point to an error in a log file or waveform file. Each chip company rolls out its own tooling and infra to deal with this—this was Kay’s entire job at his last gig. But they want to work on chips, not devtools! The solutions they come up with are often inadequate and frustrating. That’s why we started SiLogy.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e152]:
                - strong [ref=f10e153]: The solution
              - paragraph [ref=f10e154]: SiLogy is a web app to manage the entire digital verification workflow. (“Digital verification” means testing the logic of the design and includes everything before the physical design of the chip. It’s the most time-consuming stage in verification.)
              - paragraph [ref=f10e155]: "We combine three capabilities:"
              - paragraph [ref=f10e156]:
                - strong [ref=f10e157]: Test running, results, and statistics
                - text: ": Our CI tool runs tests in the cloud, allowing engineering teams unlimited flexibility in scaling their test volume. We also track each project’s progress in test coverage and test pass rate."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e158]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e159]
              - paragraph [ref=f10e160]:
                - strong [ref=f10e161]: Killer application-specific features
                - text: ": We’re building features tailored for verification use cases. We incorporate a test orchestration framework, waveform viewer, coverage report, and other features specifically for verification teams, providing customers an advantage over competitors using a generic CI solution such as Jenkins."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e162]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e163]
              - paragraph [ref=f10e164]:
                - strong [ref=f10e165]: Collaboration
                - text: ": soon you’ll be able to send a link to and leave a comment on a specific location within a log or waveform file, just like in Google Docs."
              - paragraph [ref=f10e166]:
                - img "uploaded image" [ref=f10e167]
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e168]:
                - strong [ref=f10e169]: Asks
              - paragraph [ref=f10e170]:
                - text: If you have experience with Verilog, even just from college, give our product a try at
                - link "https://dash.silogy.io/signup" [ref=f10e171]:
                  - /url: https://dash.silogy.io/signup
                - text: . Tell your loved ones who work on chip or FPGA design and verification to give us a try as well.
              - paragraph [ref=f10e172]:
                - text: If you have thoughts on the state of verification, get in touch at

                - text: Hey, we’re
                - link "Paul" [ref=f10e142]:

              - paragraph [ref=f10e147]:
                - text: Interest in designing new chips is growing, thanks to demand from AI and the predicted decline of Moore’s Law. (See this video on the
                - link "verification gap" [ref=f10e148]:

              - paragraph [ref=f10e151]: Tooling hasn’t kept up. The state-of-the-art in collaborative debugging is to walk to a coworker’s desk and point to an error in a log file or waveform file. Each chip company rolls out its own tooling and infra to deal with this—this was Kay’s entire job at his last gig. But they want to work on chips, not devtools! The solutions they come up with are often inadequate and frustrating. That’s why we started SiLogy.
              - heading [level=2] [ref=f10e152]:
                - strong [ref=f10e153]: The solution
              - paragraph [ref=f10e154]: SiLogy is a web app to manage the entire digital verification workflow. (“Digital verification” means testing the logic of the design and includes everything before the physical design of the chip. It’s the most time-consuming stage in verification.)

              - paragraph [ref=f10e156]:

              - paragraph [ref=f10e160]:
                - strong [ref=f10e161]: Killer application-specific features
